- Phi: Dual-objective interaction question; AI/HCI specific.

**[S] question · — (root edge) › Does a property survive combining objects?** — phase: (not phase-mapped) · recurrence 1 · papers: W4386081890

**[S] question · — (root edge) › Whether a process protects or harms** — phase: (not phase-mapped) · recurrence 1 · papers: W7163554174

**[S] question · — (root edge) › What explains symptom heterogeneity** — phase: (not phase-mapped) · recurrence 1 · papers: W7163554174

# 2. Link proposals

Format (§10): target edge · URL · comment = the exemplification claim (P5). Grouped by paper.

**W7163565667** — https://doi.org/10.1007/s11682-026-01167-1
- → value · — (root edge) › Measured: The authors present their efficiency account explicitly as 'one potential interpretation' and qualify connectivity claims throughout, exemplifying a measured disposition.
- → value · — (root edge) › Forthcoming: A detailed limitations discussion (design, imputation, site, vascular confounds) plus disclosure of the null performance link exemplifies forthcoming disclosure of weaknesses.
- → value · — (root edge) › Skeptical of one's own conclusions: Including age as a nuisance covariate and providing an unimputed reanalysis in the supplement shows the authors distrusting their own first result.
- → action · — (root edge) › Pressure-test your own result: Findings were stress-tested via covariate control, FDR thresholding, and a unimputed-values reanalysis before being claimed.
- → action · Pressure-test your own result › Correct for multiple comparisons: Across 17,292 ROI-to-ROI connections the authors applied a p<.05 FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg) connection threshold before reporting significance.
- → action · — (root edge) › Reuse openly shared data: The whole analysis is built on the openly shared HCP-Aging 2.0 imaging, hormone, and behavioral release rather than newly collected data.
- → action · Report it straight › Report findings that cut against your hypothesis: The authors hypothesized increased encoding connectivity and found none, and reported the null estradiol–performance correlation, reporting against their own predictions.
- → tool · Neuroimaging connectivity toolbox › CONN toolbox: ROI-to-ROI generalized psychophysiological-interaction connectivity was computed using CONN toolbox release 22.a with SPM 12.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Shared lifespan neuroimaging dataset: The study draws imaging, estradiol, and FaceName behavioral data from the Human Connectome Project – Aging 2.0 shared cohort.
- → question · — (root edge) › What drives individual differences in cognitive aging?: The introduction names the open puzzle of why some individuals decline cognitively while others do not, motivating the connectivity investigation.
- → question · — (root edge) › How do hormonal transitions reshape memory networks?: The study asks how estradiol level relates to task-modulated effective connectivity among memory regions during midlife, instantiating the hormone-and-memory-networks question.

**W7163698933** — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0349860
- → value · — (root edge) › Reflexive about one's own influence: Team members 'engaged in reflection as individuals and as a team' and recorded reflexive field notes to keep their own assumptions from shaping the analysis — the disposition enacted.
- → value · — (root edge) › Deferential to lived experience: The study's guidelines center 'youth having a say' and reducing researcher-participant power imbalances, treating youth as authorities on their own mental-health journeys.
- → value · — (root edge) › Protective of participants: Creating safe space, embedding mental-health resources in the workbook, deleting video files, and withholding raw transcripts per ethics board show care for participants taking priority over openness.
- → action · — (root edge) › Let participants choose how to take part: Youth chose their own art medium, their virtual platform, and complementary methods, and were given flexible ways and times to participate.
- → action · — (root edge) › Draw out experience through art-making: Ecomaps, journey maps, and self-chosen art pieces were used alongside interviews specifically to elicit and deepen experiences difficult to put into words.
- → action · — (root edge) › Reconcile interpretations across analysts: Authors independently coded the first 10%, computed percentage agreement and a Kappa coefficient, and debated disagreements with the larger team until consensus.
- → action · — (root edge) › Read different data forms against each other: The analysis explicitly asked what the visual data supported, challenged, or omitted relative to the textual data, comparing forms for congruence and divergence to refine themes.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Journey map: Youth built time-and-emotion journey maps with pre/during/post touchpoints to visualize the pandemic's impact on their mental health.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Ecomap: Youth drew circles for key people, places, and activities with lines graded for connection strength and quality, mapping their relational world before and after the pandemic.
- → question · — (root edge) › How does experience shift across phases of a shared disruption?: The study sought youth's mental-health journeys across pandemic time points, yielding a phased Chaos → Introspection → Personal Growth arc.
- → question · — (root edge) › How to surface experiences that exceed words?: The introduction motivates arts-based methods as a way to access nuanced, sensitive experience 'when words themselves may be difficult.'

**W2919892864** — https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01633
- → value · Rigor › Wary of taken-for-granted guarantees: The paper exists because the authors refuse to assume Poisson/GLM estimates exist by default; it shows nonexistence is a real, under-appreciated hazard for a workhorse method.
- → value · Honesty › Fair to overlooked predecessors: The authors center a 'largely uncredited' Verbeek (1989) (nine citations) and build their unifying result on it, explicitly giving due credit to forgotten work.
- → action · Pressure-test your own result › Verify estimates exist before interpreting them: The paper derives necessary-and-sufficient existence conditions and proposes a way to verify them before estimating, enacting an existence check prior to any inference.
- → action · Report it straight › Resurface neglected prior results: The authors trace and re-credit the scattered, under-cited lineage (Verbeek, Geyer, Clarkson & Jennrich, Wedderburn, Haberman) and unify it explicitly.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Pre-estimation diagnostic for model validity: The paper introduces a scalable separation-detection algorithm (iterated least-squares-with-equality-constraints) that diagnoses whether estimates exist before running the model, even with many fixed effects.
- → question · — (root edge) › Do my estimates even exist?: The paper's core inquiry is exactly when ML/PML estimates fail to exist for a broad class of GLMs and how to certify their existence.
- → question · — (root edge) › Where does a routine method silently fail?: The paper exposes how popular estimators (gamma/inverse Gaussian PML with zeros) silently break, with standard software dropping observations without justification or converging to nonsensical values.

**W7154200910** — https://doi.org/10.1145/3808279
- → value · — (root edge) › Mindful of the user's effort: The paper is driven by the observation that input labeling is cumbersome and error-prone in structure-rich domains, and designs queries explicitly to be easy to answer — enacting attention to the human's burden.
- → value · — (root edge) › Trusting formal guarantees: The authors back each design choice with theorems (optimality of query selection, correctness of convergence, correctness of separator construction), treating proof as the warrant for the method.
- → action · — (root edge) › Letting users choose rather than label: Socrates synthesizes multiple-choice queries and the user simply selects the intended behavior (a Hoare-triple cluster), replacing example annotation with selection.
- → action · — (root edge) › Framing a design tension as an optimization: Query selection is posed as argmax[DP(Q) − λ·C(Q)], turning the informativeness/interpretability tradeoff into an explicit optimization objective.
- → action · — (root edge) › Decomposing an intractable search into stages: Rather than jointly optimizing preconditions and postconditions, the method first selects ϕ then constructs ψ_i, splitting one infeasible search into two tractable subproblems.
- → tool · — (root edge) › SMT solver: The implementation uses the Z3 SMT solver for satisfiability checks and for solving the OMT and MaxSAT formulations central to precondition synthesis and separator construction.

**W4386081890** — https://doi.org/10.1007/s00025-026-02687-4
- → value · — (root edge) › Drawn to anomalies: The introduction is organized around the anomaly that synthesis holds on R yet fails on R×R, with the stated aim to 'enlighten this mysterious situation' — inquiry launched from a contradiction.
- → value · — (root edge) › Reductive: The plan to reach any LCA group from R by repeatedly adjoining Z or a compact factor reveals a preference for understanding the general object through its minimal building blocks.
- → action · — (root edge) › Reduce to known cases: Corollaries 1–2 prove the general characterization by starting from Schwartz's result on R and applying Theorem 2 and the structure theorem to reach arbitrary groups in finitely many steps.
- → action · — (root edge) › Recast as an equivalent problem: The proof replaces synthesizability with the equivalent localizability of ideals in the Fourier algebra, then works entirely in that reformulation.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Established structure theorem: The Structure Theorem of compactly generated LCA groups (R^a × Z^b × F) is used as the decomposition scaffolding that lets the induction over factors run.
- → question · — (root edge) › Does a property survive combining objects?: The paper asks whether spectral synthesis transfers to direct products, noting it does for Z but fails for R, exemplifying the preservation-under-combination question.

**W7162256314** — https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911
- → value · — (root edge) › Measured: Throughout, the authors calibrate every claim to its warrant ('we do not claim genetic canalization', 'not a uniquely diagnostic exposure', 'context-linked correlate'), exemplifying a disposition of measured assertion.
- → value · — (root edge) › Skeptical of one's own conclusions: The authors set conditions under which their own dog-cohabitation hypothesis should be rejected, exemplifying skepticism toward their favored conclusion rather than advocacy for it.
- → value · — (root edge) › Integrative across disciplines: The commentary fuses genomics, behavioural neuroscience, microbiome science, and evolutionary anthropology to surface a gap none of those fields saw alone.
- → action · — (root edge) › Make the claim falsifiable: The authors translate a sweeping conjecture into context-linked predictions with an explicit falsification criterion ('if signatures are absent... the dog-linked account is weakened or rejected').
- → action · Make the claim falsifiable › Account for competing explanations: The design requires dog co-residence to explain variance beyond diet, mobility, and pathogen burden, using within-site contrasts, negative controls, and specificity tests.
- → action · — (root edge) › Turn a fuzzy exposure into a measurable proxy: The authors operationalize 'dog companionship' into a standardized, pre-specified proxy index from faunal abundance, recurrence across layers, and household association.
- → action · — (root edge) › Stage the test from accessible to hard: The framework sequences tests: establish a reproducible modern-cohort signal first, then mount the costlier deep-time palaeoepigenetic comparison as a second stage.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Standardized exposure proxy index: The authors specify a dataset-relative scoring index (quantiles/standardized scores) to classify dog-dense vs dog-poor contexts because raw specimen counts are not comparable across sites.
- → question · — (root edge) › What shapes human regulatory biology?: The commentary is motivated by asking which social and ecological exposures calibrate human stress and immune gene regulation.
- → question · What shapes human regulatory biology? › Does cohabiting with another species leave biological marks?: The paper's core niche question is whether sustained human-dog proximity produced measurable epigenetic signatures in human populations.

**W7163554174** — https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-026-01526-5
- → value · Rigor › Wary of false positives: Treating RNAseq DEGs as provisional given its 'relatively high false discovery rate' and re-measuring 37 hits on a second platform exemplifies distrust of a single noisy measurement.
- → action · Pressure-test your own result › Confirm with an independent method: The authors validated the mRNA-sequencing differentially expressed genes with an orthogonal NanoString nCounter assay before reporting them.
- → value · Rigor › Wary of bias: Having symptom profiles assigned by psychologists 'blinded to the anatomical information' shows a standing suspicion of how knowledge of the data could sway classification.
- → action · Guard against bias › Blind raters to other data: Two psychologists categorized cases into mood/motor/mixed while blinded to anatomical information — the concrete blinding step.
- → value · Honesty › Forthcoming: The discussion volunteers the small sample size, the RNAseq false-discovery rate, and NanoString's limits in detecting low-expression transcripts as caveats on its own claims.
- → tool · Quantify gene expression › RNA sequencing: Whole-transcriptome Illumina sequencing of MCC tissue was used to discover 223 differentially expressed genes.
- → tool · Quantify gene expression › NanoString nCounter assay: The nCounter system measured a 46-gene inflammation panel to validate the sequencing results.
- → question · — (root edge) › Whether a process protects or harms: The introduction frames the study around the unresolved debate over whether neuroinflammation is protective or toxic in disease, and the results read as 'a complex combination of gain and loss of function.'
- → question · — (root edge) › What explains symptom heterogeneity: Stratifying HD cases into motor, mood, and mixed cohorts and finding motor-specific neuroinflammatory signatures pursues why one disease diverges into distinct symptom profiles.

**W7163710897** — https://doi.org/10.2196/89940
- → value · — (root edge) › Reflexive about one's own bias: A nurse-researcher explicitly frames his professional background as a source of bias to be guarded against throughout analysis, exemplifying a standing reflexive disposition.
- → action · — (root edge) › Surface one's own bias while analyzing: The conduct — 'ongoing reflexive discussions were held throughout the analytical process' plus consultation with a thematic-analysis expert — is the concrete enactment of managing insider bias during coding and theme refinement.
- → action · — (root edge) › Check interpretations with those studied: Returning transcripts to participants for confirmation of accuracy instantiates checking interpretations against the subjects' own recognition.
- → action · — (root edge) › Sample until no new themes emerge: Data collection was stopped precisely when no new categories were generated across the 10 interviews — a saturation-based stopping decision.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Semistructured interview: Individual, face-to-face semistructured interviews with a piloted, flexibly-ordered guide and adaptive follow-ups were the instrument used to elicit nurses' tacit prioritization factors.
- → question · — (root edge) › Which expert judgments resist formalization?: The study sorts elicited prioritization factors by computational tractability, concluding medical-acuity factors quantify while patient- and organization-context factors resist standardization — directly working the question of what expert judgment can be formalized.

**W4379259748** — http://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00806
- → value · — (root edge) › Drawn to the computable: The work is framed by electronic-structure calculations and proposes a numerical scheme; the relaxation is chosen precisely because it yields a finite-rank, computable object — exhibiting an orientation toward what can be calculated.
- → value · — (root edge) › Wary of one's own approximations: Rather than resting on the moment-constrained relaxation, the authors interrogate it — proving convergence to the exact Lieb functional and a rate for the ground-state energy — enacting distrust of their own shortcut.
- → action · Make a hard problem tractable › Replace a full constraint with finitely many moments: The paper replaces the full partial-trace (density) constraint on operators with M scalar moment constraints, directly producing minimizers of rank at most M+2.
- → action · — (root edge) › Prove an approximation converges to its exact target: Section 4 proves the MCAL functional converges to the exact Lieb functional as the number of moments goes to infinity, with convergence rates on the approximate ground-state energy.
- → action · — (root edge) › Import a result from a neighboring field: Tchakaloff's theorem from classical moment theory is carried into the trace-class operator / Hilbert-space setting to obtain the sparsity result.
- → tool · Representation theorem › Tchakaloff's theorem: A Tchakaloff-type proposition on Hilbert spaces is the device used to re-express the operator's eigendecomposition as a finite (K ≤ M+1) combination of pure states.

**W4403579412** — https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-026-02804-1
- → value · — (root edge) › Sparing of those studied: The work is justified by avoiding the invasive dye injection of fluorescein angiography, exemplifying a disposition to ease what the procedure costs the patient.
- → value · — (root edge) › Wary of single-dataset results: The authors are unwilling to rest on in-domain performance, instead pressing the model against ten external datasets — a wariness toward single-dataset success.
- → action · — (root edge) › Testing on external datasets: The generator is evaluated zero-shot and few-shot across ten external public datasets spanning segmentation, diagnosis, prediction, and retrieval.
- → action · — (root edge) › Validating outputs against expert judgment: Clinical experts judged the fidelity of the generated FFA videos, grounding the synthetic output in human expert assessment.
- → tool · — (root edge) › Generative adversarial network: Fundus2Video is built as an autoregressive GAN, using an adversarial generator as the instrument of video synthesis.
- → question · — (root edge) › Can a non-invasive proxy stand in for an invasive exam?: The paper asks whether color fundus images can substitute for invasive fluorescein angiography, positioning the model as a non-invasive alternative.
- → question · — (root edge) › Can one representation transfer across many tasks?: The generator's features are shown to transfer across diverse downstream tasks, testing whether one representation serves many.

# 3. Cost/benefit tunnel proposals

Format (§10): from-edge ↔ to-edge · cost/benefit relation · co-grounding document (P8) · directness (P2).

**TUN-1 [C]** · value "Skeptical of one's own conclusions" ↔ action "Pressure-test your own result"
- The disposition to distrust one's own result is paid for by the cost of running robustness/artifact checks; most direct enactment. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11682-026-01167-1

**TUN-2 [S]** · value "Skeptical of one's own conclusions" ↔ action "Make the claim falsifiable"
- Self-skepticism enacted at design time by stating a criterion that could defeat one's own favored hypothesis. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911

**TUN-3 [S]** · value "Forthcoming" ↔ action "Report findings that cut against your hypothesis"
- Being forthcoming is enacted at the cost of publishing disconfirming/null outcomes; most direct enactment. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11682-026-01167-1

**TUN-4 [S]** · value "Measured" ↔ action "Account for competing explanations"
- Calibrated assertion is bought by crediting the favored factor only after rival drivers are ruled out. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911

**TUN-5 [S]** · value "Wary of false positives" ↔ action "Confirm with an independent method"
- Wariness of false positives is discharged by re-measuring hits on an orthogonal platform. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-026-01526-5

**TUN-6 [S]** · value "Wary of bias" ↔ action "Blind raters to other data"
- Wariness of bias is enacted at the design-time cost of withholding information from raters. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-026-01526-5

**TUN-7 [S]** · value "Wary of single-dataset results" ↔ action "Testing on external datasets"
- Distrust of in-domain success is paid for by evaluating on outside data; most direct enactment. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-026-02804-1

**TUN-8 [S]** · value "Wary of one's own approximations" ↔ action "Prove an approximation converges to its exact target"
- Distrust of a surrogate is paid for by proving convergence that certifies recovery of the exact object. · co-grounded: http://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00806

**TUN-9 [S]** · value "Wary of taken-for-granted guarantees" ↔ action "Verify estimates exist before interpreting them"
- Wariness of silent guarantees is paid for by explicitly checking that estimates exist. · co-grounded: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01633

**TUN-10 [S]** · value "Fair to overlooked predecessors" ↔ action "Resurface neglected prior results"
- Fairness to predecessors is enacted at the cost of digging up and re-crediting neglected work. · co-grounded: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01633

**TUN-11 [S]** · value "Reflexive about one's own influence" ↔ action "Surface one's own bias while analyzing"
- Reflexivity is performed through ongoing explicit bias discussion during analysis; most direct enactment. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.2196/89940

**TUN-12 [S]** · value "Reflexive about one's own influence" ↔ action "Reconcile interpretations across analysts"
- Awareness of shaping the findings is purchased through independent coding and consensus that decenters any single reader. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0349860

**TUN-13 [S]** · value "Deferential to lived experience" ↔ action "Let participants choose how to take part"
- Ceding authority to the studied person is paid for by building real choice of mode into the protocol. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0349860

**TUN-14 [S]** · value "Mindful of the user's effort" ↔ action "Letting users choose rather than label"
- Caring about the human's burden is paid for by eliciting supervision through selection instead of annotation. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1145/3808279

**TUN-15 [S]** · value "Trusting formal guarantees" ↔ action "Framing a design tension as an optimization"
- Trusting proof is enacted by formalizing the goal as an objective whose solution can be proven optimal. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1145/3808279

**TUN-16 [S]** · value "Drawn to the computable" ↔ action "Replace a full constraint with finitely many moments"
- The pull toward computability is paid for by relaxing an exact constraint into a finite, sparse surrogate. · co-grounded: http://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00806

**TUN-17 [S]** · value "Reductive" ↔ action "Reduce to known cases"
- A reductive temperament is paid for by building the general result up from settled base cases. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00025-026-02687-4

**TUN-18 [S]** · question "How do hormonal transitions reshape memory networks?" ↔ tool "Shared lifespan neuroimaging dataset"
- Answering the hormone-and-memory-network question requires acquiring a large shared cohort with paired imaging and hormone data. · co-grounded: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11682-026-01167-1
